comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PHASE 1 COMPLETE (rebar-debug) — root causes proven at runtime for all three modes.

## Mode 1 — lease loss -> red CI. CONFIRMED.
`abort_check` raises `advisory.ReconcileLockLost`, whose MRO is
`ReconcileLockLost -> RuntimeError -> Exception`. It is NOT `applier.RescheduleError`,
so `run_pass`'s except arm (`__main__.py:367-375`) falls past the reschedule branch to
`return 1`. The workflow whitelists only 0/75/3, so exit 1 hits `*)` -> red.

Runtime proof (re-verified independently, not taken on trust):
    issubclass(ReconcileLockLost, RescheduleError) -> False
    run_pass(...) -> 1   with stderr byte-identical in shape to the CI log

The asymmetry is the defect: the SAME event detected BEFORE the pass returns 3 and the
workflow calls it "benign, skipping". Aborting mid-pass is correct and deliberate
(ADR 0031; ticket 2711 "pass aborts, no double-run") — no exit code was ever specified
for it. ADR 0031's own wording decides it: "a re-run is idempotent" = EXIT_RESCHEDULE (75),
already wired in the workflow as "next scheduled run will retry".
Legitimacy: incomplete-implementation (design authority cited) -> unlocks repair.

## Mode 3 — unhandled 404 aborts the whole pass. CONFIRMED, and the worst of the three.
`handle_update` soft-fails a 404; `handle_create` and `handle_delete` call their leaves
with NO try/except. `applier._apply_one` re-raises `HTTPError` ABOVE its per-mutation
backstop on the explicit assumption that "404 soft-failed in the handler" — true for 1 of 3
handlers. Injecting HTTPError(404) into each leaf:
    create : ESCAPED (pass-fatal)
    update : ISOLATED (stale-binding-404)
    delete : ESCAPED (pass-fatal)
Production impact, run 30465914822: applied 1 of 30 planned mutations, **29 valid mutations
silently skipped**. That is a direct violation of the acceptance criteria of CLOSED bug
e534-5154-2401-40fb: "no valid mutation is silently skipped".
Legitimacy: defect — an incompletely-applied prior fix. The general rule was already
written down in `apply_handlers.py` ("A 404 on a single mutation's target means the issue is
gone: this is a PER-MUTATION failure, never pass-fatal") and then applied to one handler.

## Mode 2 — push exhausts 5 retries. CONFIRMED mechanism, deferred fix (see below).
Recovered the full retry timeline from run 30585738860: all five merges SUCCEEDED and
integrated five distinct remote SHAs — the loop converges, then loses the push race each
time. Competitor arrival ~8.4s mean; backoff sleeps 3/6/10/17s, so each remote advance lands
INSIDE the corresponding sleep. Modelled P(exhaust all 5) ~= 12% per run under that burst
rate, vs ~1.7e-6 with no sleep. Exponential backoff is anti-adaptive here: after a successful
merge our HEAD is already fast-forwardable, so sleeping can only forfeit the race it is
meant to win. The workflow claims at :319 to "mirror the local client path (_store/push.py)"
— which has NO backoff and re-pushes immediately. It also computes a 5th merge and then
discards it unpushed (`:321-332`), throwing away a free ~93%-likely attempt.

## Additional CONFIRMED latent defect (not the reported symptom)
`_ref_lock._PUSH_REJECT_MARKERS = ("stale info", "rejected", "cannot lock ref")` over-matches.
I drove `_push_lease_cas` with real git stderr strings:
    server-side concurrent ref lock  -> CLASSIFIED AS CAS MISMATCH ("lease lost/stolen")
    remote internal rejection        -> CLASSIFIED AS CAS MISMATCH
    pre-receive hook declined        -> CLASSIFIED AS CAS MISMATCH
    GitHub secondary rate limit      -> CLASSIFIED AS CAS MISMATCH
    auth failed / host unresolved    -> fail-closed (correct)
This violates the module's own documented promise (`_ref_lock.py:719-722`): "a genuine
transport failure ... we do NOT classify as a CAS mismatch (fail-closed)". Worse, that branch
raises WITHOUT logging the stderr, so a production occurrence cannot be diagnosed after the
fact — which is exactly why we cannot currently tell whether the two mode-1 lease losses were
genuine takeovers or spurious. Both failures landed ~86s in, on the second heartbeat tick
(lease 120s, interval 40s), which is suspicious but unproven either way.

## Scope of the fix now in flight
Fixing modes 1 and 3 (both Python, both deterministically testable, both with cited
authority). RED oracles were written FIRST and confirmed failing for the right reason, then
held out from the implementing agent.
Modes 2 and the marker over-match are being filed as linked follow-ups rather than bundled:
mode 2 changes retry semantics of a shared push path and needs a contention harness, and the
marker narrowing changes lock classification on an occurrence that is (by the logging gap
above) currently unprovable. Sequencing them is deliberate, not dropping them — the full
quantified analysis goes on the follow-up tickets.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
EVIDENCE for the acceptance criterion "Cancellation rate is either explained as expected or reduced" — it is EXPECTED, and no work is lost.

## Measurement

Sampled 15 cancelled `Reconcile Bridge` runs via the Actions jobs API:

    sampled: 15 | cancelled-while-pending (no work): 15 | executed steps: 0 | api errors: 0

Every one had **no jobs ever created** — zero executed steps. Not a single cancelled run
had started the reconciler, touched the pass lock, mutated Jira, or written a ticket
event. A separate spot-check of 3 more recent cancellations (30592231406, 30590245682,
30588021254) gave the same result.

## Mechanism

`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` declares:

    concurrency:
      group: reconcile-bridge
      cancel-in-progress: false

`cancel-in-progress: false` means a RUNNING pass is never interrupted — it always
completes. GitHub, however, keeps at most ONE run *pending* per concurrency group: when
a newer run is queued behind an already-pending one, the older pending run is cancelled
as superseded.

The bridge feeds that queue from two sources at once — the `*/20` cron backstop and the
`RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS` re-dispatch (each run dispatching its successor). With a pass
taking minutes, arrivals routinely outpace the single-flight group, so superseded
*pending* runs are the steady state.

## Conclusion

The ~15% cancellation rate is queue collapse, not aborted work. It is the designed
behaviour of `cancel-in-progress: false` under a deliberately over-fed schedule, and it
is exactly what protects a running pass from being killed mid-flight. Reducing it would
mean either slowing the continuous loop or dropping the cron backstop — both of which
trade freshness for a cosmetically cleaner run list.

I originally listed the cancellation volume in this ticket's description as a possible
common driver behind modes 1 and 2. That inference is now RETRACTED: a run that never
starts cannot contend for the pass lock or the tickets branch, so cancellations cannot
be causing either failure mode. The real driver of contention is the continuous
re-dispatch producing overlapping *successful* runs, which is a separate matter and is
covered by 4c4f-e554-849a-4dfd.

Criterion satisfied as "explained as expected". No change proposed.

## Summary

The `Reconcile Bridge` workflow fails in production on a recurring basis — **22
failed runs between 2026-07-23T20:29Z and 2026-07-30T22:14Z** — and **7 of those
failures landed AFTER the most recent reconciler-bridge bug fix**, including two
in the very `refs/reconciler/lock` subsystem that fix repaired.

Individual failures are self-healing (a later scheduled run succeeds), which is
why they have never been ticketed: the heartbeat canary only files a ticket when
staleness exceeds its 2h threshold (it did so once, `4b5c`). The remaining
failures are invisible.

## Timing investigation vs commit history

**Most recent reconciler-bridge bug fix:** `7c763f1a7` —
*"a4b2: prune an orphaned local pass-lock ref"*, authored 2026-07-27 23:20:41
-0700 = **2026-07-28T06:20:41Z**. Ticket `a4b2` (*Stranded local
refs/reconciler/lock wedges every local reconcile pass permanently*) is a **bug**
and its fix is specifically about the pass-lock ref lifecycle.

Every later commit touching `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` is J-series
Jira Data Center *story* work (`62d9`, `0a94`, `aac8`, `9fd4`), not a bug fix.
`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge*.yml` has no commit since `5623a2496`
(`0e15`, 2026-07-19); `src/rebar/_store/push.py` / `sync.py` have none since
`27e1165cd` (2026-07-17).

**Failures after that fix (7):**

| When (UTC) | Run | Failing step |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-29T15:27:11Z | 30465914822 | Run reconciler |
| 2026-07-30T00:45:55Z | 30503669644 | Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets |
| 2026-07-30T03:06:34Z | 30510284129 | Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets |
| 2026-07-30T05:02:44Z | 30515516036 | Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets |
| 2026-07-30T19:46:26Z | 30576272914 | Run reconciler |
| 2026-07-30T20:29:25Z | 30579382013 | Run reconciler |
| 2026-07-30T22:03:07Z | 30585738860 | Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets |

**Rate before vs after the fix** (same workflow, contiguous windows):

```
PRE-FIX  2026-07-23T20:29 -> 2026-07-28T06:20 : 955 runs, 815 success,  15 failure, 124 cancelled  (1.57% fail)
POST-FIX 2026-07-28T06:20 -> 2026-07-30T22:14 : 549 runs, 460 success,   7 failure,  81 cancelled  (1.28% fail)
```

The failure rate is essentially unchanged, and the lock/lease failure mode
recurs after a lock-specific fix. `a4b2` addressed a *local* stranded ref
wedging local passes; it did not address CI-side lease loss under contention.
**This bug is therefore NOT a regression of `a4b2` and not a claim that `a4b2`
is wrong — it is the residual, separate problem `a4b2` did not cover.**

## Three distinct failure modes observed post-fix

**(1) Pass-lock lease lost mid-pass** — 2 runs (30576272914, 30579382013):

```
ref-lock renew: refs/reconciler/lock CAS rejected — lease lost/stolen
  (held 52b2181c53bacdfc7c6d4623afbd5d5ec6f6b0ff)
ERROR: reconcile heartbeat lost the lease (pass_id='2026-07-30T19-50-55') — aborting pass
ERROR: reconcile_once raised: pass lock lease lost mid-pass (pass_id='2026-07-30T19-50-55') — aborting
```

Aborting on lease loss is correct-by-design (`2711`: "heartbeat loses lease
mid-pass -> pass aborts, no double-run"), but the abort surfaces as a hard
workflow failure (exit 1) rather than a benign skip.

**(2) Push to `origin/tickets` rejected after 5 retries** — 4 runs:

```
Push rejected (attempt 4):
 ! [rejected]            HEAD -> tickets (fetch first)
error: failed to push some refs to 'https://github.com/navapbc/rebar'
hint: Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do not have
Push failed after 5 retries. Last stderr: ...
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

Concurrent writers keep advancing `origin/tickets` faster than the retry budget.

**(3) Unhandled `HTTP Error 404` from the reconcile pass** — 1 run (30465914822,
2026-07-29T15:34:55Z):

```
ERROR: reconcile_once raised: HTTP Error 404: Not Found
```

Preceded in the same run by repeated (non-fatal) warnings:

```
WARNING rebar_reconciler.apply_inbound_records: _apply_inbound_update: rebar.link failed for
  761e-5af2-ed57-408a -> 119f-63e3-34b7-4f96 (blocks): RebarError('rebar link failed (exit 1):
  Error: ERROR: redundant link — ... are in a direct parent-child relationship')
```

A bare 404 escaping as an unhandled exception is the least explained of the
three and may be a genuine gap rather than contention.

## Adjacent signal: cancellation volume

124 pre-fix + 81 post-fix runs were **cancelled** (~15% of all runs), consistent
with heavy schedule/dispatch overlap. High overlap is the plausible common
driver behind both mode (1) and mode (2), so it is included here as evidence
rather than as a separate ticket.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** contention between overlapping reconciler runs is absorbed
  (backoff, longer retry budget, or a clean no-op exit), so a run that loses a
  race does not turn the workflow red; genuinely unhandled errors (mode 3) fail
  loudly and distinguishably.
- **Actual:** ~1.3% of runs fail, in three different ways that are
  indistinguishable at the workflow level, none individually tracked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each of the three modes is classified as either *benign contention*
      (should exit non-red / be absorbed) or *a real fault* (should stay red),
      with the decision recorded.
- [ ] Mode (1): losing the pass lock to a legitimate concurrent holder no longer
      produces a red run; a genuine lock fault still does.
- [ ] Mode (2): the `origin/tickets` push either succeeds under normal
      contention (adequate retry/backoff, or fetch-rebase-retry) or exits
      non-red when it has provably lost a benign race.
- [ ] Mode (3): the `HTTP Error 404` path is root-caused and either handled with
      a specific error or reported with enough context to identify the
      failing request.
- [x] Post-fix verification. The `>= 500 runs` population gate originally written
      here is **WAIVED by operator decision (2026-07-31)**: at ~215 Reconcile Bridge
      runs/day it is wall-clock-bound at ~2.3 days, and it adds no evidence about the
      MECHANISM beyond what the oracles already prove. Replaced by, and satisfied by:
      (a) each fixed mode proven RED-first against an oracle held out from the
          implementing agent, then mutation-checked by re-seeding the exact defect —
          mode 1 returns `assert 1 == 75`, mode 3's create/delete 404 escapes again;
      (b) the post-fix sample that actually exists at close, recorded plainly:
          **7 Reconcile Bridge runs** since the fix landed (6 success, 1 cancelled,
          0 failures). Seven runs is a small sample and is explicitly NOT claimed as
          proof the failure has stopped — it is on the record so the number is stated
          rather than implied. Sustained-absence evidence, if wanted, needs the
          wall-clock this waiver declines to spend.
- [ ] Cancellation rate is either explained as expected or reduced.
- [ ] File paths: `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`,
      `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` (pass lock / reconcile_once error
      handling).

## Investigation provenance

Found during a cross-source audit of AWS, Gerrit and GitHub Actions logs for
errors not tracked as bugs (2026-07-30). Run inventory: 2,598 Actions runs over
2026-07-23 → 2026-07-30 pulled via the Actions API; failure classification from
per-job step conclusions and job logs.
